cadence_spm.amendment_15_doc: Community ambulation cadence ~ N(95, 15^2) spm. Population: healthy community-dwelling adults. 2.33-sigma lower tail: 60 spm (very slow, frailty boundary). 3.0-sigma upper tail: 140 spm (brisk walk). Excluded: running (>140 spm). Traces to: cadence_spm primitive (Article I).

step_length_m.amendment_15_doc: Adult step length ~ N(0.65, 0.12^2) m. Population: healthy community-dwelling adults. Lower tail 0.25 m: very slow or frail gait. Upper tail 1.0 m: tall athletic walkers. Excluded: running stride (>1.0 m). Traces to: step_length_m primitive (Article I).

flat.amendment_15_doc: Flat CoM vertical oscillation ~ N(4.5, 1.5^2) cm. Population: healthy adults on level ground. Lower tail 1.5 cm: very stiff pathological gait. Upper tail 8.0 cm: exaggerated bounce gait. Traces to: vertical_oscillation_cm primitive (Article I).

slope.amendment_15_doc: Slope CoM vertical oscillation ~ N(4.5, 1.5^2) cm. On moderate slopes (3-15 deg) the CoM vertical oscillation per step is dominated by foot placement geometry, not slope grade, so the distribution is identical to flat. Traces to: vertical_oscillation_cm primitive (Article I).

stairs.amendment_15_doc: Stair CoM vertical oscillation ~ N(15.0, 3.0^2) cm. Physically grounded: standard UK/US residential riser height 17-22 cm -> CoM must clear this height per step. mu=15.0 cm from mean riser 18 cm minus partial CoM oscillation recovery. Lower tail 10.0 cm: low-rise steps. Upper tail 20.0 cm: high-rise industrial stairs. Traces to: vertical_oscillation_cm primitive (Article I).

flat.note: Flat terrain: zero slope by definition.

slope.amendment_15_doc: Slope angle uniform(3, 15) deg. Lower bound 3 deg: perceptible grade (ADA ramp minimum). Upper bound 15 deg: near limit of comfortable ambulation for healthy adults without assistive devices. Uniform chosen: no preferred grade within this physiological range. Traces to: vertical_oscillation_cm via acc_x_dc = G*sin(slope_rad) (Article I).

stairs.note: Stairs terrain: slope_deg fixed at 0 because IMU tilt is captured by the stair vertical oscillation model, not a continuous incline. See walker_model.py __post_init__ stair branch.

flat.amendment_15_doc: Flat stance fraction fixed at 0.60. Population consensus: healthy adult stance fraction 58-62% of gait cycle on level ground. Fixed at midpoint 0.60 to prevent covariance with cadence in training data. Traces to: cadence_spm primitive via stance_dur_s = stance_frac * (60/cadence_spm) (Article I).

slope.amendment_15_doc: Slope stance fraction fixed at 0.62. Uphill ambulation increases stance fraction by 2-4 percentage points due to increased propulsive demand. 0.62 is 2pp above flat, consistent with 10 deg reference slope in PROFILES['slope']. Traces to: cadence_spm primitive (Article I).

stairs.amendment_15_doc: Stair stance fraction fixed at 0.65. Ascending stairs requires prolonged single-limb support to clear the riser, measured at 63-67% in instrumented stair studies. 0.65 matches PROFILES['stairs']. Traces to: cadence_spm primitive (Article I).

si_stance_true_pct.amendment_15_doc: Symmetry Index ~ N(5.0, 8.0^2) pct, clipped at 0. Population: community-dwelling adults including sub-clinical asymmetry. mu=5.0 pct: mean mild asymmetry seen in general adult population (Robinson 1987 reports 10% clinical threshold; mu=5 captures sub-clinical). Upper tail 50 pct: moderate clinical pathology. Clip at 0 because SI is a magnitude (unsigned asymmetry). Traces to: cadence_spm via delta_s = SI * stance_nom_s / 200 in walker_model.py (Article I).

mounting_offset_deg.amendment_15_doc: Mounting offset ~ N(0, 5^2) deg. Population: real-world device application by patients. sigma=5 deg: expected 1-sigma variation in patient self-application. Upper/lower bound +/-15 deg: maximum before acc_x/acc_z cross-projection corrupts step detection gate. Traces to: vertical_oscillation_cm via rotation_y matrix projection in walker_model.py (Article I).

loose_fit_attenuation.amendment_15_doc: Loose fit attenuation uniform(0.75, 1.0). 1.0 = perfect coupling; 0.75 = 25% signal attenuation from loose strap. Lower bound 0.75: at attenuation below 0.75 the HS impulse drops below the 5.0 m/s^2 adaptive detection threshold for flat walker, causing step detection failure -- this is a firmware boundary, not a data-gen parameter range. Uniform chosen: no preferred fit quality within physiologically valid range. Traces to: vertical_oscillation_cm via hs_impact_ms2 attenuation in walker_model.py (Article I).

step_variability_ms.amendment_15_doc: Step timing variability ~ N(20, 10^2) ms. Population: healthy adults across terrains. mu=20 ms: typical coefficient of variation 2-5% of step period at 100 spm (600 ms period) -> sigma ~= 12-30 ms; mu=20 ms is a conservative midpoint. Upper tail 60 ms: elevated variability seen in healthy elderly or challenging terrain (matches PROFILES['stairs'] step_variability_ms=25). Traces to: cadence_spm primitive via step_period_s = 60/cadence_spm (Article I).

terrain_int.article_i_primitive: all three primitives (terrain determines primitive ranges)
terrain_int.terrain_distribution_justification: 60/20/20 split. Flat 60%: dominant real-world ambulation context; ensures PINN learns the flat reference well. Slope 20%: community ambulation includes ramps and hills (ADA: up to 8.33% grade ubiquitous). Stairs 20%: stair ascent/descent is the most discriminative terrain for the gait algorithm because vertical_oscillation_cm shifts by >10 cm, fundamentally changing every derived signal parameter. Equal slope/stairs weighting ensures the PINN does not underfit either non-flat terrain. Traces to: all three Article I primitives.
